Benefits of Generative AI in Retail 5 Use Cases for Generative AI in Retail Examples of GenAI in the Retail Industry Revolutionize Your Retail Operation with Oracle and GenAI GenAI in Retail FAQs Leading retailers are experimenting with generative AI in the hopes of solving some of the industry’s biggest problems since Richard Sears stabled his horses and wagons and started opening physical stores. They’re beginning to use GenAI to create product summaries and other website content, generate conversational responses to prompts from customers and employees, personalize their marketing, and even summarize customer feedback to help with merchandising and product innovation. However, many organizations experimenting with GenAI have seen disappointing results. This isn’t because of flaws in the technology itself, but because when GenAI’s training stops, so does its learning. Often, this results in so-called hallucinations—inaccurate or misleading results generated by GenAI models. Retailers are starting to use techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to give the model more relevant information for each prompt so it can respond more accurately to employee and customer queries. Read on to learn more about how retailers are overcoming early GenAI obstacles and finding success with pioneering applications. What Is Generative AI? Generative AI is a subset of artificial intelligence that’s capable of understanding plain language prompts or questions and responding with text or images. It’s also capable of ingesting large quantities of data and producing summaries of that content, as well as interpreting that data and making suggestions. Key Takeaways GenAI is helping retailers understand customers better based on their order histories, enabling retailers to serve more helpful responses to customer questions and create personalized shopping lists. Retailers are using GenAI to generate content such as product descriptions for online stores, catalogs, and shelf displays, as well as blog posts and personalized marketing emails. Retailers are using GenAI to take “social listening” to the next level, summarizing customer feedback across a variety of sources including social media, product review sites, and call center transcripts to create the ultimate feedback loop. Retailers are inserting GenAI-powered chatbots into the procurement process, lowering the cost of goods and freeing up personnel. Large retail chains are using GenAI to create more immersive and interactive training videos. How Will GenAI Change Retail? GenAI can change the industry by helping retailers maximize sales and profit margins with existing customers. It may even help reverse the decades-long trend of deteriorating customer loyalty by enabling retailers to provide surprisingly great customer service. For example, GenAI can help retailers achieve the following: Optimize displays. Retailers can make physical store displays more effective by combining smart display devices, conventional AI analysis of sales data, and GenAI's conversational capabilities to produce more compelling promotional copy and design elements. Improve in-store customer service. Not all employees have the innate ability to connect with customers on the floor, but anyone with a tablet can access assistance from GenAI. This tool can quickly help employees direct customers to the particular item they’re looking for and suggest related items they might be interested in buying. GenAI could even prompt employees to ask customers about themselves or what they’re looking to accomplish, which can present even more cross-selling opportunities. For example, a customer shopping for a particular interior paint at a hardware store could be led to buy paint brushes suited for that type of paint. Consolidate and summarize feedback. Retailers can use GenAI to aggregate and interpret customer feedback from a variety of internal and third-party sources, including social media sites, call center and chat transcripts, and online reviews, creating succinct summaries from hundreds or thousands of comments and suggestions. These summaries can keep management better informed about the performance of their physical and online stores—notably, customer satisfaction with the quality of service, the breadth and depth of product selection, and whether products meet expectations.
